name: real_vd_rescan_storm
description: TWO SHAPE DECISIONS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. (1) The VD lane is a bare `delta`, not a `full_resync`: a VDFirst `Cleans` session is isVD too, so it queues in the VD scan lane and waits its turn there WITHOUT scanning anything -- with 100 agents that doubled the lane's pressure for zero inventory, and a first connection has nothing to clean anyway. (2) retry.max_attempts is 120 (60s of re-sending) because 100 agents arriving at once DO saturate that lane (thousands of bare 503s from vd.capacity.503.total, one indexer connector and one scan at a time). With the default 10 attempts, ~85 VDFirst sessions exhausted their budget and the manager then correctly SKIPPED those agents' re-scans ('no package inventory available (first scan not completed yet, VDFirst will cover the updated feed)') -- the storm answered 100x 200 while only a third of the scans ran. If a target still exhausts the budget, that IS the finding: the VD scan lane, not /scan/vd, is what a 100-agent first connect hits first. 100 agents (50 Windows + 50 Linux) that first sync their WHOLE inventory - real captured FIM, syscollector, SCA and syscollector_vd payloads, each as a first-connection full_resync - and only then, once the documents have had time to land in the indexer, all ask for a vulnerability re-scan at once: POST /scan/vd {"type":"feed_update"} with the feed_offset each agent learned from /control. Two DIFFERENT manager paths in the order a real agent walks them: the VDFirst session scans the inventory it carries through inventory_sync_server's VD scan lane, then /scan/vd re-scans that same, already-indexed inventory through remoted's worker pool into the VD module. The 90s initial_delay on the scan_vd step is the gap between indexing and re-scanning; the storm itself is deliberately unshaped (requests_per_second 0), so the 100 requests arrive together and queue against a VD module that scans ONE agent at a time (ScanOrchestrator holds an exclusive lock). Sender-side the run only sees admissions (200 = queued, not scanned): the scans themselves are visible in modulesd's log as 'reason=feed_update', one per agent, distinct from the 'option=VDFirst' one its session triggered; an agent whose VDFirst never landed is skipped there instead, which is the manager being right and the run being under-provisioned. Needs a target whose CVE feed has finished loading, or every scan_vd answers 409 version_mismatch against offset 0 - see tool_simulator/docu/14-scan-vd.md.
